Leadership Styles & Employee Productivity in Indian Tech Startups

By Cyril Mani Thomas · Advisor: Prof. Inga Jēkabsone · Faculty of Engineering Economics and Management

Read the thesis

85 pages · 130 sources · written in English

About the study

A quantitative survey of 82 employees at Yejella Pvt Ltd, Hyderabad, testing how seven leadership styles relate to employee productivity in a knowledge-intensive startup environment.

  • Empowering, participative and transactional leadership showed significant positive effects on productivity.
  • Autocratic leadership had a significant negative effect (β = −0.262, p = 0.013).
  • Together the styles explain about 24.7% of productivity variance (p = 0.003).
  • Recommendations: leadership development, participative decision-making, empowerment, KPI-based monitoring and process optimisation.
